title: Japanese Ukiyo-e
description: Woodblock prints of the 'floating world' — landscapes, kabuki, and everyday Edo life.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (Kanagawa oki nami ura), also known as The Great Wave, from the series "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei)"
items.description_narrative: Katsushika Hokusai's iconic color woodblock print, 'The Great Wave,' captures a colossal wave cresting over three fishing boats, threatening to engulf them amidst a turbulent sea. In the distance, the serene form of Mount Fuji stands against the sky, anchoring this dramatic scene from his famous series 'Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji.'
items.tags: great wave, mount fuji, ukiyo-e, woodblock print, ocean, dramatic, japanese landscape

items.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (Kanagawa oki nami ura), also known as The Great Wave, from the series "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjurokkei)"
items.description_narrative: A monumental wave dominates this scene, poised to engulf fishing boats near Kanagawa, with Mount Fuji visible in the distance. This iconic work is part of Hokusai's renowned series "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji," capturing both nature's power and human vulnerability.
items.tags: wave, seascape, mount fuji, ukiyo-e, woodblock print, japanese art, dramatic, nature

items.title: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji)
items.description_narrative: Mount Fuji glows a deep vermilion under a streaked cirrus sky in this stripped-down, almost abstract composition from Hokusai's "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji." Its bold flat color and elemental simplicity make it one of the most reproduced images in Japanese art.
items.tags: hokusai, mount fuji, woodblock print, edo period, thirty-six views, landscape

items.title: Ejiri in Suruga Province
items.description_narrative: A sudden gust sends travelers' hats and loose papers whirling into the air as bent trees frame a distant Mount Fuji. The print's dynamic depiction of invisible wind, rendered purely through flying debris and straining bodies, is a tour de force of ukiyo-e design.
items.tags: hokusai, wind, mount fuji, woodblock print, edo period, humor

items.title: Kajikazawa in Kai Province
items.description_narrative: A lone fisherman balances on a rocky spit casting his line into a foam-flecked river, Mount Fuji rising serenely in the distance. The composition's dramatic diagonal current showcases Hokusai's mastery of Prussian-blue printing and dynamic asymmetry.
items.tags: hokusai, mount fuji, fishing, woodblock print, edo period, prussian blue

items.title: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge and Atake
items.description_narrative: Pedestrians dash across a wooden bridge as slanting rain streaks the sky in fine parallel lines, a barge drifting below on the Sumida River. From "One Hundred Famous Views of Edo," this print famously inspired Vincent van Gogh's own painted copy.
items.tags: hiroshige, rain, edo, bridge, woodblock print, van gogh influence

items.title: Plum Park in Kameido
items.description_narrative: A gnarled plum tree's blossoming branches cut boldly across the foreground against a pink dusk sky, with strolling visitors glimpsed beyond in Kameido's famous garden. Its radically cropped, close-up viewpoint became one of the most influential compositions for Impressionist and Post-Impressionist painters in Europe.
items.tags: hiroshige, plum blossom, edo, woodblock print, cropped composition, japonisme

items.title: Evening Snow at Kanbara
items.description_narrative: Muffled travelers trudge through a silent, snow-blanketed village beneath a pale gray sky, the thatched rooftops softened into rounded drifts. Part of "The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō," it is celebrated as one of the most poetic snow scenes in Japanese printmaking.
items.tags: hiroshige, tokaido, snow, woodblock print, edo period, travel

items.title: Three Beauties of the Present Day
items.description_narrative: Three renowned Edo beauties—a geisha and two teahouse waitresses—are arranged in a subtly triangular composition, their faces rendered with Utamaro's signature idealized elegance. The print exemplifies bijin-ga, the ukiyo-e genre devoted to celebrating fashionable women of the day.
items.tags: utamaro, bijin-ga, beauties, woodblock print, edo period, portraiture

items.title: Takiyasha the Witch and the Skeleton Spectre
items.description_narrative: A giant skeletal ghost, summoned by the sorceress-princess Takiyasha, looms through a tattered curtain to confront startled samurai intruders. This dramatic triptych, blending Western anatomical study with fantastical legend, is among the most famous supernatural images in Japanese art.
items.tags: kuniyoshi, skeleton, supernatural, triptych, woodblock print, samurai legend

items.title: Fuji from Gotenyama at Shinagawa on the Tōkaidō
items.cultural_context: Japanese, Edo period; from Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji
items.medium: Woodblock print, ink and color on paper
items.description_narrative: Crowds picnic beneath blossoming cherry trees on Goten-yama hill above Edo Bay, with Mount Fuji floating in the distance. The hill was a favorite spring flower-viewing spot along the great Tokaido highway.

items.title: Watermill at Onden
items.cultural_context: Japanese, Edo period; from Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji
items.medium: Woodblock print, ink and color on paper
items.description_narrative: Villagers wash rice and draw water at a great turning waterwheel on the Shibuya River, in what is now central Tokyo, beneath a distant Mount Fuji. The scene is an idyll of the rhythms of rural labor.

items.title: Shōno: Driving Rain
items.cultural_context: Japanese, Edo period; from The Fifty-Three Stations of the Tōkaidō
items.medium: Woodblock print, ink and color on paper
items.description_narrative: Travelers and palanquin-bearers scramble up a hill through a sudden downpour rendered in slashing diagonal lines of rain and bent bamboo. It is often called the finest print in Hiroshige's celebrated series of the Tokaido road.

items.title: Yui: Satta Pass
items.cultural_context: Japanese, Edo period; from The Fifty-Three Stations of the Tōkaidō
items.medium: Woodblock print, ink and color on paper
items.description_narrative: Tiny travelers cling to a vertiginous cliff path high above Suruga Bay, gazing across the water toward Mount Fuji. The once-perilous Satta Pass offered one of the most spectacular views on the entire Tokaido road.

items.title: Fireworks at Ryōgoku
items.cultural_context: Japanese, Edo period; from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
items.medium: Woodblock print, ink and color on paper
items.description_narrative: Crowds throng Ryogoku Bridge and pleasure boats fill the Sumida River as fireworks burst against the deep summer night. The scene captures one of Edo's most beloved seasonal spectacles.

items.title: Kinryūzan Temple, Asakusa
items.cultural_context: Japanese, Edo period; from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
items.medium: Woodblock print, ink and color on paper
items.description_narrative: A giant red paper lantern of the Kaminarimon gate fills the foreground as snow drifts over the approach to Senso-ji temple. The dramatic contrast of vast near object and tiny distant scene is a signature Hiroshige device.

items.title: Naniwaya Okita
items.medium: Woodblock print, ink and color on paper
items.description_narrative: A bust-length portrait of Okita, the celebrated waitress of the Naniwaya teahouse near Asakusa, set against a shimmering mica ground. Utamaro's idealized 'large-head' beauties turned real Edo women into popular celebrities.

items.title: Zhang Shun, the White Stripe in the Waves
items.cultural_context: Japanese, Edo period; from One Hundred and Eight Heroes of the Water Margin
items.medium: Woodblock print, ink and color on paper
items.description_narrative: The tattooed hero Zhang Shun plunges through churning water locked in combat, his inked body twisting against the foam. Kuniyoshi's heroic Suikoden warriors sparked a craze for pictorial tattooing across Edo.

items.title: The Moon on Musashi Plain
items.cultural_context: Japanese, Meiji period; from One Hundred Aspects of the Moon
items.medium: Woodblock print, ink and color on paper
items.description_narrative: A white fox stares out from windblown silver pampas grass beneath a full moon on the vast Musashi plain. It is among the most poetic and atmospheric designs of Yoshitoshi's late masterwork series.

items.title: Tsuchigumo (The Ground Spider)
items.description_narrative: The legendary Earth Spider assails a company of samurai in a swirl of webs and shadow. It comes from Thirty-Six Ghosts, Yoshitoshi's final major series on the supernatural.
items.tags: spider, yokai, samurai, supernatural, ukiyo-e, night

items.title: Woman Passing a Roadside Shop Near Oji
items.description_narrative: A woman walks past a modest roadside shop in Oji, a scenic district north of Edo known for its inns and cherry blossoms. The print is held by the Cleveland Museum of Art.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, Edo period, genre scene, Oji, Cleveland Museum of Art

items.title: Kamakura no Gengoro Seizing Torinoumi Tasaburo
items.description_narrative: This dramatic warrior print depicts the legendary strongman Kamakura no Gengoro grappling with his rival Torinoumi Tasaburo, a popular subject drawn from samurai legend. The print is held by the Cleveland Museum of Art.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, warrior print, samurai legend, Cleveland Museum of Art

items.title: Women and Children Walking Along the Sumida River
items.description_narrative: Figures stroll along the banks of the Sumida River, a favorite subject for Hokusai and his contemporaries as a site of leisure just outside Edo. The print belongs to the Cleveland Museum of Art.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, Sumida River, genre scene, Cleveland Museum of Art

items.title: Group of Figures near a Brook
items.description_narrative: A gathering of figures relaxes beside a small brook in a quiet landscape scene typical of Hokusai's genre prints. The work is held by the Cleveland Museum of Art.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, landscape, genre scene, Cleveland Museum of Art

items.title: The Six Immortal Poets (Rokkasen)
items.description_narrative: The 'Rokkasen' were six celebrated waka poets of the 9th century, a favorite subject for ukiyo-e artists to depict together in scenes of literary refinement. This print is held in the Library of Congress collection.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, Rokkasen, classical poets, Library of Congress

items.title: Rice Planters
items.description_narrative: Farm workers bend to plant rice seedlings in a flooded paddy field, one of Hokusai's many prints documenting the daily labor of rural Japanese life. The print is held by the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, rural life, agriculture, Rijksmuseum

items.title: Sailing on the Sumida River
items.description_narrative: Boats carry passengers along the Sumida River, one of Edo's most popular waterways for both commerce and leisure travel. The print is held by the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, Sumida River, boats, Rijksmuseum

items.title: Balloon Flower and Dragonfly
items.description_narrative: A balloon flower blossom and a hovering dragonfly are rendered with close botanical observation, part of Hokusai's extensive output of nature studies. The print belongs to the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, nature study, flowers, dragonfly, Rijksmuseum

items.title: Battling Warriors
items.description_narrative: Two warriors clash in combat in this action-filled print drawing on the martial themes popular in Edo-period illustrated fiction. It is held by the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, warrior print, combat, Rijksmuseum

items.title: Shishi (Lion-Dog)
items.description_narrative: A shishi, the mythical lion-dog guardian figure of Japanese and Chinese tradition, is depicted in a dynamic, stylized pose. The print is held in the Library of Congress collection.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, shishi, mythical creature, Library of Congress

items.title: Two Women with a Doll
items.description_narrative: Two women examine a doll together in a domestic genre scene, a subject reflecting everyday leisure activities of Edo-period women. The print is held by the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, genre scene, domestic life, Rijksmuseum

items.title: Shibaura
items.description_narrative: This print depicts Shibaura, a coastal district of Edo known for its shoreline views and fishing activity. It is held in the Library of Congress collection.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, Shibaura, coastal view, Library of Congress

items.title: Playing Sugoroku in the Third Month (Yayoi)
items.description_narrative: Figures play sugoroku, a traditional board game, during Yayoi, the third month of the lunar calendar associated with early spring. The print is held by the Ishikawa Prefectural Museum of Traditional Arts and Crafts in Kanazawa.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, sugoroku, board game, seasonal scene

items.title: Man Lifting a Sake Barrel
items.description_narrative: A laborer hoists a heavy sake barrel overhead, a study of physical strength and everyday commerce in Edo-period Japan. The print is held in the Library of Congress collection.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, genre scene, labor, Library of Congress

items.title: The Mirror Polisher (Kagamitogi)
items.description_narrative: A tradesman polishes a mirror in this scene drawn from Noroma kyogen, a genre of comic theatrical interludes performed alongside puppet plays. The print is held by the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, kyogen theater, genre scene, Rijksmuseum

items.title: Chinese Boys Learning to Write and Paint
items.description_narrative: Young boys practice calligraphy and painting under supervision, a subject drawn from the Chinese-influenced genre of 'karako' (Chinese children) imagery popular in Edo-period art. The print is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, karako, calligraphy, Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Nanukayo (The Seventh Night)
items.description_narrative: This print, titled 'Nanukayo' (The Seventh Night), depicts a wave-filled scene associated with the seventh night of the seventh month, tied to the Tanabata star festival. It is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, Tanabata, wave, seasonal scene, Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Imadogawa
items.description_narrative: This print depicts Imadogawa, a stretch of the Sumida River near the Imado district of Edo, an area popular for its ferry crossings and riverside teahouses. It is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: Ukiyo-e, Imadogawa, Sumida River, Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Fukagawa Lumberyards
items.description_narrative: Piled log rafts and timber yards line the canals of the Fukagawa lumber district on the eastern edge of Edo, framed by a snow-dusted embankment. The scene captures the timber trade that supplied the rapidly rebuilding wooden city after its frequent fires.
items.tags: fukagawa, lumberyard, timber, canal, snow, edo

items.title: Nihonbashi Bridge: Clearing Weather after Snow
items.description_narrative: Fish sellers and porters cross the snow-covered Nihonbashi Bridge, the starting point of Edo's five great highways, as the sky clears over the shogunal city. Edo Castle's watchtowers rise faintly on the horizon beyond the Nihonbashi River.
items.tags: nihonbashi, bridge, snow, edo castle, fish market, winter

items.title: Tsukudajima from Eitai Bridge
items.description_narrative: Fishing boats gather near Tsukudajima island as it is seen from the great arc of Eitai Bridge spanning the Sumida River. The island's fishing community, granted land by the shogunate, supplied Edo's markets with fresh catch.
items.tags: tsukudajima, eitai bridge, sumida river, fishing boats, edo bay

items.title: Ueno Yamashita
items.description_narrative: Shops and teahouses crowd the base of Ueno hill in the district known as Yamashita, a lively commercial quarter beneath the temples of Kan'ei-ji. Pedestrians and merchants animate the street below the hillside's greenery.
items.tags: ueno, yamashita, shops, street scene, kaneiji, edo

items.title: Mount Atago in Shiba
items.description_narrative: Visitors climb the steep stone stairway of Atago Hill in the Shiba district to reach the shrine at its summit, a popular vantage point over Edo Bay. Pine trees frame the view from the hill's crest across the rooftops of the city below.
items.tags: atago hill, shiba, shrine, stairway, edo bay, pine trees

items.title: Night View of Matsuchiyama and the San'ya Canal
items.description_narrative: A crescent moon hangs over the wooded rise of Matsuchiyama as boats glide along the San'ya Canal below in the blue dusk. The hill's Shoten shrine and the nearby Yoshiwara pleasure quarter made this a favored nocturnal subject.
items.tags: matsuchiyama, sanya canal, night view, moon, sumida river, boats

items.title: View from Massaki of Suijin Grove, the Uchigawa Inlet, and Sekiya Village
items.description_narrative: A framed pine bough and a red-lacquered fence in the foreground open onto a broad view across the Sumida River toward the sacred grove of Suijin Shrine and the rice fields of Sekiya village. The composition's dramatic close foreground set against a flat, distant landscape is a signature device of the series.
items.tags: massaki, suijin shrine, sumida river, sekiya, pine tree, landscape

items.title: The Armor-Hanging Pine at Hakkei Slope
items.description_narrative: An ancient, gnarled pine associated with a legend of the warrior Minamoto no Yoshiie hanging his armor on its branches stands beside the road at Hakkei Slope in Omori. Travelers pass beneath the famous tree on their way along the Tokaido highway.
items.tags: hakkeizaka, armor pine, omori, tokaido, legend, pine tree

items.title: Five Pines, Onagi Canal
items.description_narrative: Weathered pine trees, said to share a single root, stand at the edge of the Onagi Canal in eastern Edo, a spot noted for this unusual grove. Boats pass quietly along the waterway beneath the trees' distinctive silhouette.
items.tags: onagi canal, five pines, edo, waterway, boats, trees

items.title: The City Flourishing, the Tanabata Festival
items.description_narrative: Tall bamboo poles strung with colorful paper streamers and decorations rise above the rooftops of a merchant district in celebration of the Tanabata star festival. Mount Fuji appears faintly in the distance beyond the festive banners.
items.tags: tanabata festival, bamboo, streamers, mount fuji, edo rooftops, summer

items.title: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ohashi Bridge and Atake
items.description_narrative: Pedestrians hurry across Shin-Ohashi Bridge, hunched under umbrellas and straw rain capes, as a sudden downpour sweeps over the Sumida River toward the Atake district. Sheets of rain rendered with fine diagonal woodblock lines make this one of the series' most celebrated compositions.
items.tags: shin-ohashi bridge, rain, sumida river, atake, umbrellas, downpour

items.title: Yatsumi Bridge
items.description_narrative: From Yatsumi Bridge, so named because eight other bridges could reportedly be seen from its span, boats and waterside buildings stretch along the canals of central Edo. The print showcases the dense network of waterways that served as the city's commercial arteries.
items.tags: yatsumi bridge, canal, edo waterways, boats, bridges, cityscape

items.title: Dawn Inside the Yoshiwara
items.description_narrative: Rows of cherry trees in blossom line the main street of the Yoshiwara pleasure quarter as dawn breaks over the district's teahouses. The scene captures the quarter during its famous spring display, when trees were temporarily transplanted in for the season.
items.tags: yoshiwara, dawn, cherry blossoms, pleasure quarter, edo, spring

items.title: New Fuji, Meguro
items.description_narrative: Visitors climb a man-made replica of Mount Fuji built in the Meguro district, offering worshippers who could not travel to the real mountain a substitute pilgrimage. The actual Mount Fuji rises pale in the distance beyond the artificial hill.
items.tags: meguro, mount fuji, fuji replica, pilgrimage, hill, edo

items.title: Suruga-cho
items.description_narrative: The gabled roofline of the Echigoya dry-goods store lines a bustling street in the Suruga-cho district, with Mount Fuji framed symmetrically at the end of the avenue. The street took its name from the clear view it once afforded of Suruga Province's famous peak.
items.tags: suruga-cho, mount fuji, echigoya, street scene, shops, edo

items.title: Hibiya and Soto-Sakurada from Yamashita-cho
items.description_narrative: Snow blankets the daimyo residences and moats of the Hibiya and Soto-Sakurada districts near Edo Castle, seen from Yamashita-cho. The high stone walls and pine-topped embankments mark the boundary of the shogun's inner administrative quarter.
items.tags: hibiya, sakurada, edo castle, daimyo residences, snow, moat

items.title: Temple Gardens in Nippori
items.description_narrative: Manicured garden grounds surround the temples of Nippori, a district nicknamed 'Higurashi no Sato,' or 'the village where you forget the time of day,' for its scenic beauty. Visitors stroll among clipped pines and garden pavilions set against the hillside.
items.tags: nippori, temple garden, higurashi, pines, edo, garden pavilion

items.title: Suwa Bluff in Nippori
items.description_narrative: Visitors gather on Suwa Bluff, a hilltop shrine precinct in Nippori prized for its panoramic view over the fields and villages north of Edo. Teahouses along the bluff catered to travelers pausing to enjoy the outlook.
items.tags: nippori, suwa bluff, hilltop view, shrine, edo outskirts, panorama

items.title: Shops with Cotton Goods in Odenma-cho
items.description_narrative: Bolts of dyed cotton cloth hang in the storefronts of Odenma-cho, a wholesale textile district near Nihonbashi. Porters and clerks move briskly along the street, evoking the ward's importance to Edo's cloth trade.
items.tags: odenmacho, cotton textiles, wholesale district, edo commerce, cloth shops

items.title: Suijin Grove and Massaki on the Sumida River
items.description_narrative: Boats drift along the Sumida River past the wooded shrine grove of Suijin and the riverside village of Massaki, a scenic stretch popular for its shrine dedicated to the god of water. The low horizon and broad river emphasize the openness of the northern outskirts of Edo.
items.tags: sumida river, suijin shrine, massaki, riverboats, shrine grove

items.title: Flower Park and Dango-zaka Slope in Sendagi
items.description_narrative: Terraced flower gardens climb the slope of Dango-zaka in Sendagi, a suburb known for elaborate seasonal chrysanthemum displays. Visitors wind up the hillside path past the garden's blooms toward the teahouses at its summit.
items.tags: sendagi, dangozaka, flower garden, chrysanthemums, hillside, edo suburb

items.title: The Kawaguchi Ferry and Zenkoji Temple
items.description_narrative: A ferry carries passengers across the Arakawa River at Kawaguchi, with the roof of Zenkoji Temple visible on the far bank. The crossing linked Edo's northern outskirts to the farming villages beyond the river.
items.tags: kawaguchi ferry, zenkoji temple, arakawa river, ferry crossing, edo outskirts

items.title: Kiyomizu Hall and Shinobazu Pond at Ueno
items.description_narrative: The hexagonal Kiyomizu Kannon Hall, modeled after its namesake in Kyoto, overlooks Shinobazu Pond and its lotus-covered surface from a hillside in Ueno. A round pine, trained into a distinctive loop, frames the temple in the foreground.
items.tags: ueno, kiyomizu hall, shinobazu pond, lotus, temple, pine

items.title: Chiyogaike Pond in Meguro
items.description_narrative: A quiet pond in the rural Meguro district, said to be named for a court lady, is bordered by trees and a footbridge in this tranquil suburban view. The scene reflects the semi-rural character of Edo's southwestern outskirts before their later development.
items.tags: meguro, chiyogaike pond, footbridge, edo suburb, rural landscape

items.title: Shitaya Hirokoji
items.description_narrative: Crowds and palanquins move along the broad avenue of Shitaya Hirokoji, a firebreak boulevard created after a major Edo fire that grew into a bustling commercial strip. Shop awnings and signboards line the wide street beneath a view toward Ueno hill.
items.tags: shitaya, hirokoji, firebreak, avenue, edo commerce, ueno

items.title: Kasumigaseki
items.description_narrative: Two facing rows of daimyo mansion gates line the elevated street of Kasumigaseki near Edo Castle, with Mount Fuji and Edo Bay visible in the distance beyond the rooftops. The composition uses the converging gates to draw the eye toward the far horizon.
items.tags: kasumigaseki, daimyo gates, edo castle, mount fuji, edo bay

items.title: Plum Orchard in Kamata
items.description_narrative: Rows of blossoming plum trees fill a garden in the rural village of Kamata south of Edo, a rival destination to the more famous Kameido plum garden. Visitors stroll beneath the trees' early spring blooms in the mild afternoon light.
items.tags: kamata, plum orchard, blossoms, spring, edo suburb, garden

items.title: Azuma Shrine Grove and the Entwined Catalpa Trees
items.description_narrative: Two catalpa trees whose trunks have grown together, regarded as an auspicious symbol of marital harmony, stand within the sacred grove of Azuma Shrine east of the Sumida River. Pilgrims visited the shrine grove to see the unusual entwined trees.
items.tags: azuma shrine, entwined trees, catalpa, sacred grove, sumida river, pilgrimage

items.title: Towboats on the Yotsugi-dori Canal
items.description_narrative: Workers haul boats by rope along the narrow Yotsugi-dori Canal, an irrigation waterway running through the farmland east of the Sumida River. The straight canal and towpath recede into flat, open countryside at Edo's rural edge.
items.tags: yotsugi canal, towboats, irrigation canal, farmland, edo outskirts

items.title: Moto-Hachiman Shrine in Sunamura
items.description_narrative: The precinct of Moto-Hachiman Shrine in the village of Sunamura, southeast of Edo, is shown amid open fields near the coast. The shrine, an earlier site of the Tomioka Hachiman cult, drew visitors to this quiet coastal village.
items.tags: sunamura, moto-hachiman shrine, edo coast, shrine precinct, rural village

items.title: View to the North from Asukayama
items.description_narrative: Visitors atop the cherry-tree-covered hill of Asukayama, a public park established for blossom viewing, look out over rice fields stretching toward the mountains north of Edo. The hill was a favorite spring destination for townspeople.
items.tags: asukayama, hilltop view, cherry blossoms, rice fields, edo outskirts

items.title: The Original Fuji in Meguro
items.description_narrative: A smaller, older artificial Fuji mound in Meguro, predating the 'New Fuji' built nearby, rises above a rural roadside lined with modest dwellings. The mound allowed local worshippers a symbolic ascent of the sacred mountain.
items.tags: meguro, fuji mound, pilgrimage, edo suburb, rural road

items.title: Palace Hill in Shinagawa
items.description_narrative: Cherry blossoms cover Goten-yama, 'Palace Hill,' a scenic bluff above Shinagawa where a shogunal villa once stood, overlooking Edo Bay and the Tokaido highway below. The hill was a well-known blossom-viewing spot at the southern entrance to the city.
items.tags: shinagawa, goten-yama, cherry blossoms, edo bay, tokaido, hilltop

items.title: Hiroo on the Furukawa River
items.description_narrative: A quiet bend of the Furukawa River winds through the semi-rural district of Hiroo on the western outskirts of Edo. Modest riverside dwellings and greenery line the banks in this pastoral view.
items.tags: hiroo, furukawa river, edo outskirts, riverside, rural landscape

items.title: Yatsukoji, Inside Sujikai Gate
items.description_narrative: A wide plaza inside Sujikai Gate, where eight roads converged, teems with pedestrians, stalls, and a corner watchtower in this bustling crossroads scene near Kanda. The gate marked a major checkpoint on the routes leading into central Edo.
items.tags: sujikai gate, yatsukoji, crossroads, edo checkpoint, kanda, plaza

items.title: Kilns and the Hashiba Ferry on the Sumida River
items.description_narrative: Smoke rises from roof-tile kilns along the bank of the Sumida River near the Hashiba ferry crossing, north of Edo's built-up center. Boats ferry passengers across the river past the industrial riverside scene.
items.tags: hashiba ferry, sumida river, tile kilns, riverside industry, edo outskirts

items.title: Dam on the Otonashi River at Oji
items.description_narrative: Water rushes over a wooden dam on the Otonashi River at Oji, a spot popularly nicknamed 'the waterfall' despite being an artificial weir. The rustic mill buildings and rushing water made this a favored scenic and recreational spot north of Edo.
items.tags: oji, otonashi river, dam, weir, mill, edo outskirts

items.title: Ekoin Temple in Ryogoku and Moto-Yanagi Bridge
items.description_narrative: The rooftops of Ekoin Temple, built to memorialize victims of Edo's great fires and disasters, rise above the Ryogoku district near the Sumida River, with Moto-Yanagi Bridge crossing a canal in the foreground. The area around the temple was also famous for sumo tournaments held on its grounds.
items.tags: ryogoku, ekoin temple, moto-yanagi bridge, sumida river, edo

items.title: The Oji Inari Shrine
items.description_narrative: Steep steps lead up a wooded hillside to the Oji Inari Shrine, famed in Edo folklore as the gathering place of foxes from across the Kanto region on New Year's Eve. Worshippers ascend the shrine's forested approach beneath tall trees.
items.tags: oji inari shrine, foxes, folklore, shrine steps, edo, new year

items.title: Sunrise at Kanda Myojin Shrine
items.description_narrative: Dawn light spreads over the hillside precinct of Kanda Myojin Shrine, one of Edo's most important tutelary shrines, as the city awakens below. A torii gate and shrine buildings are silhouetted against the brightening sky.
items.tags: kanda myojin shrine, sunrise, torii gate, edo, dawn

items.title: Hatsune Riding Ground in Bakuro-cho
items.description_narrative: Horses and grooms occupy the Hatsune riding ground in the Bakuro-cho district, a training and exercise field within a busy commercial quarter of Edo. Inns and wholesale shops associated with the horse trade bordered the open grounds.
items.tags: bakurocho, hatsune riding ground, horses, edo commerce, training grounds

items.title: Yanagishima
items.description_narrative: Willow trees line the banks of a canal at Yanagishima, 'Willow Island,' a scenic spot near the Sumida River popular for its restaurants and river views. A curved wooden bridge and moored boats complete this tranquil waterside scene.
items.tags: yanagishima, willow trees, canal, sumida river, edo
